name: TheDream.US National Scholarship
description: Covers tuition and fees up to $33,000 toward a bachelor's degree at a Partner College, plus a stipend of up to $6,000 for books, supplies, and transportation. Open to first-generation immigrant students who are undocumented, with or without DACA or TPS, who entered the U.S. before age 16 and before November 1, 2020. The application round typically opens in November and closes at the end of February; the 2026-27 round closed February 28, 2026.

eligibility.immigration_status: Undocumented, with or without DACA or TPS; first-generation immigrant
eligibility.arrival: Entered the U.S. before age 16 and before November 1, 2020
eligibility.financial_need: Significant unmet need; must not be receiving or eligible for the Federal Pell Grant
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time associate or bachelor's program at a TheDream.US Partner College

requirements.proof_of_status: Documentation of immigration status and U.S. entry date
requirements.partner_college: Must enroll at an approved Partner College

name: TheDream.US Opportunity Scholarship
description: Provides up to $100,000 toward a bachelor's degree, covering tuition, fees, on-campus housing, and meals for students who live in one of 22 'locked-out' states that bar undocumented students from in-state tuition or state aid. Recipients must relocate and live on campus at an out-of-state Partner College. The round typically opens in November and closes in early February; the 2026-27 round closed February 2, 2026.

eligibility.immigration_status: Undocumented, with or without DACA or TPS; first-generation immigrant
eligibility.arrival: Came to the U.S. before November 1, 2020 and entered before age 16
eligibility.financial_need: Significant unmet need; cannot receive the Federal Pell Grant
eligibility.residency: Must graduate from high school in one of the 22 locked-out states
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time bachelor's program; must relocate and live on campus at a Partner College

requirements.relocation: Must move out of state to attend a Partner College

name: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
provider_name: Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans
description: Provides up to $90,000 in funding for full-time graduate or professional study in the United States, awarded to immigrants and the children of immigrants. Applicants must be 30 or younger and may apply while applying to graduate school or during the first two years of their program. The program does not consider school, GPA, or test score ranges for eligibility.

eligibility.enrollment: Full-time graduate or professional degree at an accredited U.S. institution
eligibility.timing: Applying to graduate school, or in the first two years of the program

name: HSF Scholar Program
description: Awards of $500 to $5,000 based on relative need, plus career services, mentorship, and leadership development for selected Scholars. Open to students of all races who identify as being of Hispanic heritage and who are U.S. citizens, permanent legal residents, or DACA recipients. The application typically opens in early January and closes in mid-February; the 2026-27 cycle closed February 15, 2026.

eligibility.ethnicity: Of Hispanic heritage; open to students of all races
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, permanent legal resident, or DACA recipient
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at an accredited public or not-for-profit four-year university or graduate school in the U.S.

name: McDonald's HACER National Scholarship
description: Tiered scholarship program for Hispanic and Latino students pursuing postsecondary education, with roughly 30 awards each year ranging from $5,000 up to $100,000 across three tiers. The program was created to help narrow the college affordability gap for Hispanic and Latino college-bound students. Applications typically open in the fall and close in late February.

eligibility.enrollment: Plan to enroll in a postsecondary institution

name: LULAC National Scholarship Fund
provider_name: League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) / LNESC
description: Awards distributed through participating local LULAC Councils in three categories: National Scholastic Achievement Awards of $2,000, Honors Awards of $500 to $2,000, and General Awards of $250 to $1,000. Applicants must have a participating LULAC Council in their area to be eligible, so students should check the Council list before applying. The application period typically closes March 31 and recipients are notified by councils by June 15.

eligibility.ethnicity: Open to all students; program serves the Hispanic community
eligibility.council_requirement: Must have a participating LULAC Council in the applicant's area
eligibility.enrollment: Enrolled or accepted at a college, university, or graduate school

requirements.application: Application submitted through a participating LULAC Council

name: TMCF Eastern Area Links Finish Line Scholarship (2026-2027)
description: Awards up to $1,500 for the 2026-2027 academic year in a single fall installment to 75 undergraduate seniors at one of 16 designated HBCU member institutions. Applicants submit a two-minute video essay describing how they embody core values for creating positive community change. Applications opened June 1, 2026.

eligibility.school_type: One of 16 designated TMCF HBCU member institutions
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident

name: TMCF Lowe's Gap Scholarship (2026-2027)
description: Awards up to $5,000 for the 2026-2027 academic year to full-time undergraduates at TMCF member institutions who are majoring in business or a STEM field. Applicants must submit a two-minute video addressing how they plan to create positive change in their community and career field. Applications opened June 1, 2026.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident

name: TMCF Enterprise Access HBCU Scholarship (2027-2028)
description: Awards up to $15,000 for the 2027-2028 academic year, distributed in two installments across fall 2027 and spring 2028, to full-time undergraduates at TMCF member HBCUs, HBCCs, PBIs, and medical or law schools. Open to all majors, with a FAFSA on file required at the time of selection. Applications opened August 3, 2026.

eligibility.school_type: TMCF member HBCU, HBCC, PBI, medical or law school
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident

name: TMCF Enterprise Access HBCC Scholarship (2027-2028)
description: Awards up to $1,500 for the 2027-2028 academic year to 34 full-time students attending TMCF historically Black community college (HBCC) member schools. Open to all majors, with a two-minute video response about using education to create impact. Applications opened August 3, 2026.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident

name: TMCF McDonald's Black and Positively Golden Scholarship (2027-2028)
description: Awards up to $15,000 for the 2027-2028 academic year, distributed in two installments across fall 2027 and spring 2028, to full-time undergraduates at TMCF's 57 publicly supported historically Black colleges and universities. Selection weighs demonstrated leadership ability alongside financial need. Applications opened August 3, 2026.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident

name: TMCF MolsonCoors Scholarship (2027-2028)
description: Awards up to $8,200 for the 2027-2028 academic year in a single payment during the fall 2027 semester to full-time undergraduates at TMCF member institutions. Open to all majors, with a 2027-2028 FAFSA required on file at the time of selection. Applications opened August 3, 2026.

eligibility.school_type: TMCF member institution (HBCU, HBCC, PBI, medical or law school)
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident

name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
description: Awards 20 four-year scholarships of $40,000 each ($10,000 per year) to Black and African American high school seniors who excel academically and demonstrate financial need. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents. The application opens after September 3 of the applicant's senior year with a December 1 deadline.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or permanent resident visa card holder

name: APIA Scholars Scholarship
description: Awards range from one-time $2,500 scholarships to multi-year $20,000 awards for undergraduates at U.S. accredited colleges and universities, with a focus on students living at or below the poverty level and those who are first in their family to attend college. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, nationals, or legal permanent residents; citizens of the Marshall Islands, Micronesia, and Palau are also eligible. The application typically opens in mid-November and closes in mid-January.

eligibility.ethnicity: Asian and Pacific Islander American focus
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, national, or legal permanent resident; also citizens of the Marshall Islands, Micronesia, and Palau
eligibility.enrollment: Enrolling or continuing as an undergraduate at a U.S. accredited college or university
eligibility.financial_need: Strong focus on students at or below the poverty level

name: Banatao Family Filipino American Education Fund
description: Awards $5,000 annually, renewable for up to four years for a total of $20,000, to rising college freshmen of Filipino heritage majoring in a STEM field. Applicants must be California residents with at least a 3.0 GPA and demonstrated financial need. Applications for 2026 are closed and reopen in 2027.

name: Shui Kuen and Allen Chin Scholarship
description: Awards $1,000 to $2,000 to undergraduate students with a connection to an Asian-owned restaurant and involvement in social justice advocacy. Requires a 3.0 GPA and demonstrated financial need, with no citizenship requirement. Applications for 2026 are closed and reopen in 2027.

eligibility.connection: Applicant or family member works or worked in an Asian-owned restaurant

name: Hsiao Memorial Social Sciences Scholarship
description: Awards $1,000 exclusively to graduate students studying social sciences or economics, with preference given to applicants of Asian heritage. Requires a minimum 3.0 GPA and demonstrated financial need. Applications for 2026 are closed and reopen in 2027.

eligibility.ethnicity: Preference for applicants of Asian heritage

name: Helen and L.S. Wong Memorial Scholarship
description: Awards $1,000 to $3,000 to rising college freshmen from Fairfield or Suisun City, California who are of at least 50 percent Asian heritage. Requires a minimum 2.8 GPA and demonstrated financial need. Applications for 2026 are closed and reopen in 2027.

name: Full Circle Scholarship
description: The American Indian College Fund's primary scholarship program for Native American students, with awards that vary but average between $2,000 and $3,000. Open to any Native American U.S. citizen who is an enrolled member or descendant of an enrolled member of a state or federally recognized tribe, with a minimum 2.0 GPA. Applications open February 1 in anticipation of the fall term, with priority review for submissions by May 31.

eligibility.tribal_status: Enrolled member or descendant of an enrolled member of a state or federally recognized tribe
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at a nonprofit, accredited college or university

requirements.application: Online application via the American Indian College Fund portal

name: Cobell Undergraduate Scholarship
description: Awards up to $5,000 for new applicants and up to $8,000 for returning applicants pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree. Open to enrolled members of a U.S. federally recognized American Indian tribe or Alaska Native corporation attending accredited nonprofit institutions. There is no minimum GPA, though a 3.25 or higher is considered competitive; the application opens December 15 and closes March 31, and recipients must reapply each year.

eligibility.tribal_status: Enrolled member of a U.S. federally recognized American Indian tribe or Alaska Native corporation
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time, degree-seeking (part-time considered case-by-case)
eligibility.gpa_note: No minimum GPA; 3.25 or higher considered competitive

requirements.references: Reference due approximately one week after the deadline

name: Point Foundation Access Scholarship
description: A $1,500 scholarship for LGBTQ+ and ally students who are first-generation college students and/or come from low-income backgrounds. Requires at least half-time enrollment in an associate or bachelor's program with the intention to enroll for the full academic year, a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA, and demonstrated connection to the LGBTQ+ and ally community. The application opens January 28 and closes March 12.

eligibility.identity: LGBTQ+ or ally with demonstrated community connection
eligibility.enrollment: At least half-time in an associate or bachelor's program

name: Point Foundation Community College Scholarship
description: A $4,800 scholarship covering fall 2026 through spring 2027 for LGBTQ+ and ally students enrolled in an associate degree program at an accredited, not-for-profit U.S. institution. Requires a minimum 2.5 GPA, at least half-time enrollment with plans to complete a full academic year, and demonstrated commitment to the LGBTQ+ and ally community. Fully online programs are excluded; the application opens January 28 and closes April 9.

eligibility.identity: LGBTQ+ or ally with demonstrated community connection
eligibility.enrollment: At least half-time in an associate degree program at an accredited not-for-profit U.S. institution
eligibility.exclusions: Fully online programs are not eligible

name: P.E.O. Program for Continuing Education Grant
description: A need-based grant of up to $4,000 for women in the United States and Canada whose education has been interrupted and who need to return to school to complete a degree or certification that improves their marketable skills for employment. Applicants must be recommended by a local P.E.O. chapter. Grants are awarded on a rolling basis through chapters rather than a single national deadline.

eligibility.circumstance: Education has been interrupted; returning to school
eligibility.purpose: Degree or certification improving marketable employment skills
eligibility.sponsorship: Must be recommended by a local P.E.O. chapter

requirements.application: Application submitted through a local P.E.O. chapter

name: P.E.O. STAR Scholarship
description: A one-time $2,500 scholarship for exceptional women in their final year of high school, recommended by a local P.E.O. chapter. Selection recognizes excellence in leadership, academics, extracurricular activities, community service, and potential for future success. Candidates must be recommended by a P.E.O. chapter to qualify.

eligibility.sponsorship: Must be recommended by a local P.E.O. chapter
eligibility.criteria: Leadership, academics, extracurricular activities, community service

requirements.application: Application submitted through a local P.E.O. chapter

name: P.E.O. Scholar Awards
description: Merit-based awards of up to $25,000 for women in the United States and Canada pursuing a doctoral-level degree at an accredited college or university. Candidates must be recommended by a local P.E.O. chapter. Awards support women at advanced stages of doctoral study.

eligibility.sponsorship: Must be recommended by a local P.E.O. chapter

requirements.application: Application submitted through a local P.E.O. chapter

name: AAHD Frederick J. Krause Scholarship on Health and Disability
provider_name: American Association on Health and Disability
description: Scholarships generally of $1,000 for students with a disability as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act, with preference for those studying public health, health promotion, disability studies, disability research, rehabilitation engineering, audiology, disability policy, or special education. Undergraduate applicants must be full-time with at least sophomore standing; graduate applicants may study part- or full-time. The 2025-2026 deadline was March 6, 2026, and the next application period opens by November 2026.

eligibility.disability: Must have a disability as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act, verified by a specialist
eligibility.field_of_study: Preference for public health, health promotion, disability studies, disability research, rehabilitation engineering, audiology, disability policy, or special education
eligibility.classification: Undergraduates must be full-time with sophomore standing or higher; graduate students may be part- or full-time
eligibility.exclusions: High school graduates entering college for the first time are ineligible

name: Anne Ford Scholarship
description: A $10,000 scholarship paid as $2,500 per year over four years for a student with a documented learning disability enrolling in a full-time bachelor's degree program. Students with autism, ADHD, or physical disabilities who also have a learning disability are eligible for consideration. Applications open in October and close in early spring; the most recent cycle was reviewed on a rolling basis until May 10, 2026.

eligibility.disability: Documented learning disability; students with autism, ADHD, or physical disabilities who also have a learning disability are eligible
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time bachelor's degree program
eligibility.criteria: Demonstrated desire to give back and serve others

name: National Federation of the Blind Scholarship Program
description: Awards 30 merit-based scholarships ranging from $3,000 to $12,000 each year to students who are legally blind in both eyes. Applicants must reside in the United States, the District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico and be pursuing full-time postsecondary study in a degree program at a U.S. institution. Applications are due by March 31 of the year in which the scholarship is awarded.

eligibility.residency: United States, District of Columbia, or Puerto Rico
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time postsecondary degree program at a U.S. institution
eligibility.age: Must be at least 18 by the summer convention
eligibility.criteria: Academic excellence, community service, and financial need

requirements.interview: Interview with a state affiliate representative

name: George H. Nofer Scholarship for Law and Public Policy
provider_name: AG Bell Association for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
description: Awards $5,000 each year to up to three full-time graduate students attending an accredited law school or pursuing graduate study in public policy. Applicants must document bilateral hearing loss in the moderately-severe to profound range and use listening and spoken language. The application typically opens in December and closes in early March.

eligibility.disability: Bilateral hearing loss in the moderately-severe to profound range; uses listening and spoken language
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at an accredited law school or graduate public policy program

name: Foster Love Family Fellowship
description: Provides up to $12,000 per year for up to five years covering tuition, books, essential school supplies, and housing allowances during the academic year, along with mentorship and a peer network. Open to former foster youth ages 18 to 24 who hold a high school diploma or equivalent and are accepted to an accredited public or nonprofit college pursuing a full-time bachelor's degree. The application historically opens in March and closes in early May; the next round opens in 2027.

eligibility.foster_care: Lived in public or private foster care for at least 12 consecutive months up to and including the 18th birthday; adopted or placed in legal guardianship from foster care after age 13; or orphaned for at least one year at the time of the 18th birthday
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time bachelor's degree at an accredited public or nonprofit college or university

name: Foster Love American Industries Trade Scholarship
description: Provides up to $12,000 in academic funding over two years to help current and former foster youth earn a trade certification or vocational degree. The scholarship targets students entering skilled trades rather than traditional four-year degree paths. The application deadline has historically fallen in early May.

eligibility.enrollment: Pursuing a trade certification or vocational degree

name: Foster Love BrandSource Scholarship
description: Provides $12,000 in academic funding for current and former foster youth pursuing higher education. Sponsored by BrandSource in partnership with Foster Love, the award supports tuition and related educational costs. The application deadline has historically fallen in late May.

eligibility.enrollment: Enrolled or accepted at an accredited institution

name: Folds of Honor Higher Education Scholarship
description: Need-based scholarships for dependents and spouses of fallen or disabled U.S. service members, awarded against unmet need for tuition, fees, on-campus housing, meal plans, and required textbooks. The maximum payment is $2,500 per term for full-time students and $1,250 per term for part-time students. The application window runs February 1 through March 31 each year, with award notifications emailed July 31.

eligibility.military_connection: Dependent or spouse of a fallen or disabled U.S. service member
eligibility.financial_need: Award based on unmet need after other aid
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time or part-time at an eligible institution

requirements.application: Online application via the Folds of Honor CommunityForce portal

name: Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
description: Need-based scholarships of up to $40,000 over four years for children and stepchildren of active duty, Reserve, or veteran U.S. Marines, and of Navy Corpsmen, Chaplains, or Religious Program Specialists attached to a Marine unit. Children of the Fallen receive $30,000 over four years and Children of the Wounded receive up to $40,000 over four years. Eligibility requires a family adjusted gross income at or below the published cap and a minimum 2.0 GPA; the application is open annually from January 1 until March 1.

eligibility.military_connection: Child or stepchild of an active duty, Reserve, or veteran U.S. Marine, or of a U.S. Navy Corpsman, Chaplain, or Religious Program Specialist attached to a Marine unit
eligibility.discharge: Veterans must have received an honorable discharge
eligibility.income_cap: Family adjusted gross income of $129,000 or less for the 2024 tax year
eligibility.institution: Accredited school eligible for federal funding

requirements.application: Online Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation application

name: AMVETS National Scholarship Program
description: Need-based scholarships of up to $12,000 for veterans, active duty service members including National Guard and Reserves, and their spouses, children, and grandchildren pursuing an undergraduate degree. Applicants must demonstrate financial need and must not be in default on a federal student loan. Graduate applicants are not eligible; the application deadline has historically fallen at the end of April.

eligibility.military_connection: Veteran, active duty service member including National Guard and Reserves, or their spouse, child, or grandchild
eligibility.enrollment: Enrolled or accepted in an undergraduate degree program at an accredited four-year college or university
eligibility.exclusions: Graduate applicants ineligible; must not be in default on a federal student loan

name: ThanksUSA Scholarship Program
description: Need-based scholarships of up to $3,000, or the full amount of program costs if lower, for dependent children age 24 or younger of U.S. military service personnel and for military spouses. Recipients must be enrolled or planning to enroll as full-time undergraduate students at a college, university, community college, or vocational-technical school. Applications are administered by Scholarship America and have historically closed in mid-May.

eligibility.military_connection: Dependent child age 24 or younger of U.S. military service personnel, or a military spouse
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time undergraduate at a college, university, community college, or vocational-technical school
eligibility.financial_need: Academic merit and financial need are considered

requirements.application: Online application via the Scholarship America ThanksUSA program site

name: Scholarships for Military Children
description: Awards a minimum of one $2,000 scholarship at each commissary location worldwide, with more than one awarded at some commissaries. Open to children of active duty, Reserve, and retired military members who meet the program's eligibility criteria. Scholarship grants are normally mailed to recipients in late July.

eligibility.military_connection: Child of an active duty, Reserve, or retired military member
eligibility.commissary: Awards are tied to a commissary location

requirements.application: Online application via the Scholarships for Military Children program

name: Children of Fallen Patriots Foundation Scholarship
description: Provides college scholarships and educational counseling to military children who lost a parent in the line of duty, covering tuition and fees, books and supplies, living expenses, and a one-time $1,650 computer stipend. Lifetime funding caps are $75,000 for Chapter 33 (Fry) students and $100,000 for Chapter 35 (DEA) students. Enrollment is open on a rolling basis and applications are reviewed monthly.

eligibility.military_connection: Child of a service member who died in the line of duty in the Air Force, Army, Coast Guard, Marine Corps, National Guard, Navy, or Space Force
eligibility.enrollment: Vocational, two-year, or four-year college or university

requirements.application: Online enrollment form or printable mail-in version

name: Pat Tillman Foundation Tillman Scholars
description: Awards averaging $10,000 per academic year to veterans, active duty service members from all branches, military spouses, and surviving spouses enrolled full-time at accredited U.S. colleges and universities. Individual amounts vary based on financial need and educational costs, and scholars join a national leadership network. The application window varies each year and can range from November to February.

eligibility.military_connection: Veteran or active duty service member from any U.S. Armed Forces branch, military spouse, or surviving spouse
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at an accredited U.S. college or university
eligibility.financial_need: Award amount varies with financial need and educational costs

name: Imagine America High School Scholarship
description: A $1,000 tuition award for graduating high school seniors attending participating career colleges, with every U.S. and Puerto Rico high school able to nominate up to five seniors each year. Selection considers likelihood of completing postsecondary education, financial need, and demonstrated voluntary community service during senior year. Applications run from September of the applicant's senior year until December 31 of the year they graduate.

eligibility.institution: Participating career college in the Imagine America High School Scholarships Program
eligibility.community_service: Demonstrated voluntary community service during senior year

requirements.high_school_nomination: Up to five seniors nominated per high school

name: Bridging the Dream Scholarship for Graduate Students
description: Awards 20 scholarships of up to $10,000 each to students enrolled in or accepted to an accredited graduate or professional degree program who demonstrate financial need and a commitment to making a positive impact in their communities. Fields supported include nursing, healthcare, law, and education. The program is administered by the Thurgood Marshall College Fund and the most recent application period ran through July 17, 2026.

eligibility.enrollment: Enrolled in or accepted to an accredited graduate or professional degree program
eligibility.criteria: Commitment to making a positive impact in their community

requirements.application: Online application administered by the Thurgood Marshall College Fund
